solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What some Christians believe in — it's taken for granted

definitions.meaning: the bodily taking up of the Virgin Mary into heaven, a doctrine held by Catholic and Orthodox Christians
a premise accepted without proof, a supposition

explanation.surface: A remark about faith: some Christians hold a belief that others simply accept without question.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine of Mary's being raised to heaven bears this name, and the same word means a supposition accepted without proof.

clue.text: Relation's adieu not hollow

indicators.note: something hollow has had its insides scooped out, so only the outer letters of each word stay

explanation.surface: A relative says goodbye, and the farewell is heartfelt rather than empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' applies to both 'adieu' and 'not', each keeping only its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a family relation, so the kinship word fits directly.

clue.text: Cut woman initially detained in sanitorium briefly

indicators.note: something detained in a place is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: san is the short form of sanatorium (spelt sanitorium here)

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that precedes it

explanation.surface: A woman is admitted to a sanatorium, and the clue says this is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawn is the past participle of saw, so it means cut, as timber cut with a saw.

clue.text: Male, strange critic, curious, putting us off electical item

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters are to be rearranged into an unusual order
putting something off removes it, so the word us is taken away from curious

explanation.surface: A man who is an odd, inquisitive critic alienates people while dealing with some electrical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting us off' takes US from CURIOUS, leaving CURIO; 'strange' then mixes CRITIC with CURIO. 'electical' is the clue's misprint for electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny integrated circuit is an electrical component, so it is an item of electrical equipment.

clue.text: Weapon from Sparta's era? Yes and no!

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Asks whether a weapon dates from ancient Sparta, answering both yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no!' hints that the weapon is and is not from Sparta's era: it is concealed in those words, but is a modern device.
explanation.definitionFit: A stun gun firing electrified darts is a weapon, used by police to incapacitate.

clue.text: Award is supported by African party, state's ultimate homage

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supported by another sits above it

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour or award
ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

indicators.note: ultimate points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An honour is backed by an African political party, and this is a state's ultimate tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour; 'state's ultimate' is the last letter of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of respect such as a bow, so it means homage or deference.

clue.text: Son, one easily fooled, complacent

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a dupe

explanation.surface: Someone's son is a dupe who is nonetheless self-satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Being self-satisfied and pleased with oneself is synonymous with complacency.

clue.text: Handy work?

parts.note: plays on handiwork: work done on the hands, trimming and shaping fingernails

explanation.definitionFit: Treating the hands and nails cosmetically is literally work on hands, hence handy work.

clue.text: Blame husband taken in by devious George, earth scientist

indicators.note: a piece taken in by another is enclosed by it
devious suggests something twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: rap, as in taking the rap, means blame

explanation.surface: A wife blames her husband after being deceived by a cunning man named George, who is a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges GEORGE to GEOGER, which then takes in RAP and H.
explanation.definitionFit: One who studies the earth's physical features and regions is a scientist of the earth.

clue.text: Northeastern ne'er-do-well cornering special constable — he's seen on TV

indicators.note: to corner someone is to hem them in, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a waster is an idle good-for-nothing
SC is the abbreviation for special constable, a volunteer police officer in Britain

explanation.surface: A northern layabout traps a part-time police officer, and the man ends up appearing on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter who reads the news on air is a person viewers see on television.

clue.text: Data from rainforest

indicators.note: from indicates the letters are drawn out of the word that follows

explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal short form of information, which means data or facts.

clue.text: Horse friends brought up is featured in country air?

indicators.note: something featured in another appears within it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: allies are friends or supporters

explanation.surface: A horse whose friends have raised it appears in some rural tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country air' looks rustic, but it means a nation's song: the anthem of France.
explanation.definitionFit: This is France's national anthem, an air or tune belonging to a country.

clue.text: Newly married, scorn one using traditional movement?

indicators.note: newly suggests making something afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newlywed scorns someone who sticks to old-fashioned ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traditional movement' sounds like a political or social cause but means an English folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of English folk dancing with bells and sticks uses customary steps, traditional movement.

clue.text: Genuine servant welcoming doctor's team

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: a piece welcoming another takes it in, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a maid is a female servant
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A true servant greets the doctor's group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish club is a famous football team from the capital of Spain.

clue.text: Organised soccer wars — they frighten some

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Arranged battles between football fans scare some people.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures set in fields to frighten birds, they literally scare some creatures.

clue.text: Referring to old Greek group of states, 151, in front of clergyman

parts.note: the EU, European Union, is a group of member states
151 in Roman numerals is CLI
a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a Greek political grouping with a number of members and a priest at its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' places the earlier pieces before the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek mathematician, so the adjective means relating to him and his geometry.

clue.text: Professorship a piece of cake? Relax here

parts.note: a piece of cake is something easy
a chair is a professor's post at a university

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a professor's post is a soft option, then invites one to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable armchair is a place where one sits back and relaxes.

clue.text: Feature of some trains really aiding passengers at front

definitions.text: Feature of some trains really aiding passengers

indicators.note: at front points to the opening letter of each of the words listed

explanation.surface: Describes something on some trains that genuinely helps the people travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the hanging loop that standing travellers hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging loop for standing travellers to grip is a fitting on some trains that helps riders.

clue.text: Something to sing after end of wonderful year in charge

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A song to perform after a marvellous year spent leading something.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of a song are what a singer performs, so they are something to sing.

clue.text: Entente is renewed in French town

indicators.note: renewed means made again, so the letters are reformed into a new word

explanation.surface: A cordial Anglo-French understanding is revived in a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: This industrial city in the Loire region is a town in France.

clue.text: Extremely cold group here up north?

parts.note: arctic means freezing, extremely cold
a circle is a group of people, such as a circle of friends

explanation.surface: A frozen gathering of people is located somewhere far to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: This line of latitude encircles the polar region, so it is found far up north.

clue.text: Drops painter home at end of class

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a common abbreviation for an artist
in means at home

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An artist heads home when a lesson finishes, and lets things fall.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to rain is to fall in drops, so to drop or pour down.

clue.text: One regularly aberrant?

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Asks about someone who habitually misbehaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a badly behaved child is often deviant.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilt, unruly child misbehaves habitually, a frequent deviant from good conduct.

clue.text: Author wrong not to finish

indicators.note: not allowed to finish, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: amiss means wrong or awry

explanation.surface: A writer is mistaken about not completing a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley and his son Martin were both British novelists, hence an author's surname.

clue.text: On return secure space

indicators.note: on return means going back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to secure it

explanation.surface: Coming back, one secures a spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Room is a synonym of space, as in having room to move.

clue.text: Leading couples in Palace cite fine, crusading, imperial area

indicators.note: leading couples means the first two letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A palace imposes a penalty on a crusading imperial power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading couples in' takes the first two letters of each word, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: The lands bordering the Pacific Ocean form a geopolitical region, an area of the world.

clue.text: Lawyer with quiet style

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A lawyer with an understated manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means flair or panache, a stylish verve.

clue.text: Booklet supports changes City introduced

indicators.note: introduced means put into something, so one piece goes inside the other
changes means alters the order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A booklet backs the changes that the financial district has brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SUPPORTS to PROSPTUS, and EC is introduced into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospectus is a printed brochure describing a school or share offer, a booklet.
